context: 4 Conclusions We conclude with a few open problems. What is the tight dependence on ε > 0 for the size of a (3p+ ε)-spanner for n bichromatic points in the plane? We have proved an upper bounds of O( 1/ε · n) in the plane, and 2n − 3 (i.e., no dependence on ε) on the line. The lightness of a spanner H for an edge-weighted graph G is the ratio w(H)/w(MST(G)) of the weight of the spanner to the weight of a minimum spanning tree of G. On bichromatic points on the line, we have shown (Proposition 10) that there is a 7-spanner of lightness 1. It remains an open to obtain upper bounds for stretch 3 ≤ t < 7 on the line, and for any t > 3 in the plane. Our results give existential bounds on the size of a bichromatic spanners. The corresponding optimization problems remain open: For a given bichromatic point set S = R ∪ B and stretch t ≥ 1, find a t-spanner of K(R, S) of minimum size or minimum weight (note that for a given instance, stretch 1 ≤ t < 3 can be feasible). We conjecture that these problems are NP-hard already in Euclidean plane. Finding good approximations is left for future research. For monochromatic spanners in the plane, these optimization problems are known to be NP-hard, and bicriteria approximation algorithms were obtained only recently [24]. However, for bichromatic points, the optimization problem is already open for n red-blue points on the line with stretch 1 < t < 7.
